investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable for 140–148 seconds. The Kubernetes scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and producing no evidence output whatsoever.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The other 4 nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence — causing a complete contract gap and a fail status on all three remote-agent checks. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, which may indicate a cluster topology change (node labels removed, nodes replaced, or node pool scaled down) that reduced the eligible node count from a larger set to only 2.

Tertiary — VM cleanup failure from prior eval runs: if withCleanup (seen in run-status-probes.mjs:1883) did not successfully release kata.peerpods.io/vm resources from previous probe executions, those slots would remain consumed and unavailable for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event: a brief node pressure event or node restart could have temporarily reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the run; this would be disproved if the check passes on a subsequent run without any intervention.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-22T10:59–11:04Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never schedules, the agent is never created, and the eval runner never reaches the state-polling logic that would produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that match the kata.peerpods.io/vm node selector have exhausted their VM resource quota (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes and preemption is not applicable on the 4 mismatched nodes. The pod remains Unschedulable for ~140–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval times out. This is an infrastructure-layer failure in the production Kubernetes cluster's kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or its contracts. This is an eval-observed infrastructure signal; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.

investigation.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (code: billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has reached its configured billing hard limit. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985), the upstream OpenAI image generation API rejected the request with error type "billing_limit_user_error" and code "billing_hard_limit_reached". The AURA backend correctly propagated this as a generation_error SSE frame (evidence: failed-check.evidence), which means no generation_completed frame was ever emitted and no image URL was produced. This is an external dependency / account configuration failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or the image generation stream routing logic. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure scoped to the observability probe environment.
proof: failed-check.message: The check message contains the verbatim OpenAI error body: {"error":{"message":"Billing hard limit has been reached.","type":"billing_limit_user_error","param":null,"code":"billing_hard_limit_reached"}}.

failed-check.evidence: The SSE frame sequence is [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message]. The generation_error frame carries code GENERATION_FAILED and the full OpenAI billing error message. No generation_completed frame appears anywhere in the sequence.
failed-check.evidence: imageUrlPresent is false, consistent with the stream never reaching a completion payload because the upstream call was rejected before image synthesis could complete.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=838 — the call returned in under one second, consistent with an immediate API-layer rejection rather than a timeout or a slow generation failure.

expected-output.contract: The contract requires frameTypes to contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent to equal true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 339-344). Neither assertion was satisfied.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1978-1986: The runner calls apiSse against /api/generate/image/stream using model process.env.AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL || "gpt-image-2", confirming the OpenAI image model is the upstream dependency that returned the billing error.
possibleCauses: Primary — OpenAI account billing hard limit exhausted: The API key or account used by the eval runner environment has hit its spending cap. This is the direct cause stated in the OpenAI error response (billing_hard_limit_reached) and is fully consistent with the sub-second rejection latency and the generation_error frame content.

Secondary — Wrong or expired API key scoped to a low-limit account: The eval runner may be using an API key associated with a restricted or trial account whose hard limit is lower than expected, causing it to exhaust faster than anticipated.

Tertiary — Eval runner environment variable AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL or the API key credential is misconfigured, routing requests to an account with a different billing profile than intended (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1986 shows the model is read from process.env.AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL).

investigations.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (code: billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame, causing both required contract assertions to fail: frameTypes did not contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent remained false.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has reached its configured billing hard limit. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1977-1985), the upstream OpenAI image generation API rejected the request with error type "billing_limit_user_error" and code "billing_hard_limit_reached". The AURA backend correctly propagated this as a generation_error SSE frame (evidence: failed-check.evidence), which means no generation_completed frame was ever emitted and no image URL was produced. This is an external dependency / account configuration failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or the image generation stream routing logic. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure scoped to the observability probe environment.
proof: failed-check.message: The check message contains the verbatim OpenAI error body: {"error":{"message":"Billing hard limit has been reached.","type":"billing_limit_user_error","param":null,"code":"billing_hard_limit_reached"}}.

failed-check.evidence: The SSE frame sequence is [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message]. The generation_error frame carries code GENERATION_FAILED and the full OpenAI billing error message. No generation_completed frame appears anywhere in the sequence.
failed-check.evidence: imageUrlPresent is false, consistent with the stream never reaching a completion payload because the upstream call was rejected before image synthesis could complete.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=838 — the call returned in under one second, consistent with an immediate API-layer rejection rather than a timeout or a slow generation failure.

expected-output.contract: The contract requires frameTypes to contain "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent to equal true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 339-344). Neither assertion was satisfied.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1978-1986: The runner calls apiSse against /api/generate/image/stream using model process.env.AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL || "gpt-image-2", confirming the OpenAI image model is the upstream dependency that returned the billing error.
possibleCauses: Primary — OpenAI account billing hard limit exhausted: The API key or account used by the eval runner environment has hit its spending cap. This is the direct cause stated in the OpenAI error response (billing_hard_limit_reached) and is fully consistent with the sub-second rejection latency and the generation_error frame content.

Secondary — Wrong or expired API key scoped to a low-limit account: The eval runner may be using an API key associated with a restricted or trial account whose hard limit is lower than expected, causing it to exhaust faster than anticipated.

Tertiary — Eval runner environment variable AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL or the API key credential is misconfigured, routing requests to an account with a different billing profile than intended (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1986 shows the model is read from process.env.AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL).

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returned HTTP 502 due to upstream Anthropic 429 rate-limit error
investigations.summary: The model-matrix smoke-test check failed because the aura-gpt-5-5 model probe received a 502 Bad Gateway from the AURA runtime harness, which itself was caused by an Anthropic API 429 Too Many Requests (rate_limit_error) response. One of two configured models (aura-claude-sonnet-4-6) passed cleanly; only aura-gpt-5-5 failed, causing the allPassed and failedModelCount assertions to be violated.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502 for the aura-gpt-5-5 model at eval run time (2026-07-22T10:54:56–10:56:26Z). The 502 body explicitly identifies the internal cause as a rate_limit_error from the Anthropic API (HTTP 429), with the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This is a transient upstream provider rate-limit condition surfaced through AURA's harness gateway, not a code defect in the eval runner or its configuration. The eval infrastructure correctly detected and recorded the failure; the violated assertions (allPassed=false, failedModelCount=1) are accurate reflections of the runtime outcome.

failed-check.evidence: results[0] (aura-claude-sonnet-4-6) ok=true, messageSample='hello from aura' — confirms the eval runner and harness path are functional for at least one model

failed-check.evidence: failedModels=['aura-gpt-5-5'], failedModelCount=1, allPassed=false — all three violated assertions trace to the single model failure

expected-output.contract: assertions require allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 333–334); both are violated solely because of the aura-gpt-5-5 502/429 response
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=89209, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold (source.check-config.model-matrix), so the failure is not a latency violation
possibleCauses: Transient Anthropic API rate-limit (429) on the aura-gpt-5-5 provider path at the time of the eval run — highest evidence strength, directly stated in the 502 error body (failed-check.evidence)

Sustained or recurring rate-limit quota exhaustion on the AURA harness account for the aura-gpt-5-5 model specifically, which would cause repeated failures across runs — lower evidence strength, no run history available to confirm (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0)

Misconfiguration of the aura-gpt-5-5 model entry causing it to route through an Anthropic provider path that is subject to tighter rate limits than the aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 path — speculative, not directly evidenced by the packet

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable for 140–148 seconds. The Kubernetes scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector, leaving zero viable scheduling targets and producing no evidence output whatsoever.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The other 4 nodes are excluded by affinity rules and cannot be used even via preemption. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence — causing a complete contract gap and a fail status on all three remote-agent checks. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 140s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=141882 endedAt=2026-07-22T10:59:04.090Z — the check ran to its full timeout before failing.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured, confirming the pod never reached a schedulable state.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=152864, also zero evidence.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler message, latencyMs=147833, also zero evidence — all three checks share the same underlying scheduling failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — the agent creation call is the first infrastructure touch point and is where scheduling is triggered.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:256-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never scheduled.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie VMs from prior eval runs have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, which may indicate a cluster topology change (node labels removed, nodes replaced, or node pool scaled down) that reduced the eligible node count from a larger set to only 2.

Tertiary — VM cleanup failure from prior eval runs: if withCleanup (seen in run-status-probes.mjs:1883) did not successfully release kata.peerpods.io/vm resources from previous probe executions, those slots would remain consumed and unavailable for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event: a brief node pressure event or node restart could have temporarily reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity at the time of the run; this would be disproved if the check passes on a subsequent run without any intervention.
